q: Dicky […] made his best pace to a recess in a back street, there to examine his pogues; for though the uxter was gone from them, they might yet bring a few coppers from Mr Weech, if they were of good quality.
1896, Arthur Morrison, A Child of the Jago:
Reportedly he is, too, rather free with his 'uxter' — that's money, Watson — which inclines the locals to look favourably on him.
